chunks: Said their apostles: "Can there be doubt about God, the originator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you to forgive some of your sins, and give you respite for a time ordained." They said: "You are only men like us, and yet you wish to turn us away from what our fathers worshipped. Bring to us then a clear proof."

key_terms.فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: Originator of the heavens and the earth

ai.seo_question: What was the response of the disbelievers when the prophets invited them to worship Allah alone?
ai.summary: In the Shia exegetical tradition, this verse highlights the tension between divine authority and human skepticism, where the people's demand for a 'clear proof' (sulṭān mubīn) often refers to the Prophet Muhammad or the Imams as the living evidence of God. The promise of forgiveness and delay until an appointed term (ajal musammā) underscores the concept of divine patience (ḥilm) before the final reckoning. This dialogue serves as a paradigm for the recurring theme of rejecting monotheism despite clear signs, a motif frequently cited in Shia sermons to illustrate the stubbornness of disbelievers.
